html:
A series of three clashes at sea between Iceland and Britain, between 1958 and 1976, over fishing rights in the waters around Iceland. Iceland won each time.

Fish were nearly all of Iceland's exports, and British trawlers from ports such as Hull and Grimsby had fished off its coasts for centuries. Iceland pushed its fishing limit out in steps:

  • to 12 nautical miles in 1958;
  • to 50 miles in 1972;
  • to 200 miles in 1975.

Each time British trawlers kept fishing, and the Royal Navy sent frigates to protect them. Icelandic coast guard ships cut the trawlers' nets with special cutters, and ships rammed. There were injuries and one death, but no real war.

Iceland's strongest card was the American base at Keflavík, key to watching Soviet submarines in the North Atlantic during the Cold War. Iceland threatened to leave NATO, and Britain's allies pressed it to give way. In 1976 Britain accepted the 200 mile zone.

The 200 mile zone soon became the world norm under the law of the sea.
sum: A series of three clashes at sea between Iceland and Britain, between 1958 and 1976, over fishing rights in the waters around Iceland. Iceland won each time.
